{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Overloaded baseline visit with many procedures",
      "quote": "BL V2 D1 (Day 1)",
      "page": 62,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The baseline visit (V2) includes a large number of procedures: randomization, injection training, study drug administration, multiple PROs, investigator assessments, safety labs, and more. This may be burdensome for patients and staff, risking incomplete data.",
      "fix": "Consider splitting some procedures (e.g., PROs) to a pre-baseline visit or reducing non-essential assessments at baseline."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patch testing requires 3 additional visits during screening",
      "quote": "Patients will be called to the site for 3 visits for the patch testing",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Patch testing adds three extra site visits during screening, increasing patient burden and potential dropout before randomization.",
      "fix": "Consider using historical patch test results more broadly or reducing the number of required readings."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent visit numbering and day labels",
      "quote": "V3 W2 D15 (Day 22)",
      "page": 62,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The visit labels are inconsistent: V3 is labeled 'W2 D15' but also '(Day 22)', which is confusing and may lead to scheduling errors.",
      "fix": "Standardize visit labels to use either study day or week consistently, not both with conflicting numbers."
    },
    {
      "title": "Tight window for PV5 visit",
      "quote": "PV51 W6 D43 ±3 (Day 78)",
      "page": 62,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The PV5 visit has a ±3 day window, which is tight for a visit at week 6, especially if patients have scheduling conflicts.",
      "fix": "Consider widening the window to ±5 or ±7 days to reduce patient burden and improve compliance."
    },
    {
      "title": "Daily diary assessments may be burdensome",
      "quote": "Patient assessment of hand and foot pruritus intensity using NRS via diary (daily)",
      "page": 62,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Requiring daily diary entries for pruritus NRS for the entire study duration may lead to poor compliance and missing data.",
      "fix": "Consider limiting daily diary to a subset of days or using electronic reminders to improve compliance."
    },
    {
      "title": "Injection training/observation at multiple visits may be unnecessary",
      "quote": "Injection training/ observation",
      "page": 62,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Injection training/observation is scheduled at V2, V3, V4, V6, V8, and EOT, which may be excessive if patients are trained early and demonstrate competence.",
      "fix": "Reduce training/observation to the first few visits and only as needed thereafter."
    },
    {
      "title": "Study drug dispensation at unscheduled and ET visits may complicate accountability",
      "quote": "Study drug dispensation",
      "page": 62,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Dispensation at unscheduled and early termination visits is not clearly defined, which may lead to confusion and accountability issues.",
      "fix": "Clarify conditions for dispensation at unscheduled/ET visits and ensure accountability procedures are followed."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patch testing washout for topical therapies may delay screening",
      "quote": "1 week for TCS/TCI /topical JAK inhibitor/crisaborole application",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The 1-week washout for topical therapies before patch testing may prolong the screening period and increase patient burden.",
      "fix": "Consider allowing patch testing before washout or shortening washout if clinically acceptable."
    }
  ]
}
